segmenti.tekst: نحن نقص عليك أحسن القصص بما أوحينا إليك هذا القرآن وإن كنت من قبله لمن الغافلين. الحمد لله رب العالمين، والصلاة والسلام على نبينا محمد وعلى آله وصحبه أجمعين. We continue with the tafsir (commentary) of Surah Yusuf. After Yusuf was locked up in prison, two more young men came in with him.
Two young men who, in prison, saw strange dreams. And these two young men were: one of them was the king's cupbearer, and the other was a cook.

We mentioned that they had been offered money, or something else, to poison the king. To poison the king. The cupbearer refused, and the cook accepted. But the king was left confused, since the cupbearer said: "Do not eat that food, it is poisoned," and then the cook came and told the king: "Do not drink that drink, it is poisonous."

So then the king was left confused: who is telling the truth now? And so he imprisoned them until it could be investigated who was right. And they had dreams: one dreamt that he was pressing grapes to make wine, and the other dreamt that there was bread above his head and that birds were eating from that bread. So they came to Yusuf, alayhis-salatu was-salam (peace be upon him).
Yusuf, alayhis-salam – what does Yusuf do? Yusuf does not answer their question directly, that is, he does not start interpreting the dreams straight away.

Rather, Yusuf says: there is something more important than that, there is something more important than interpreting dreams. So Yusuf took the opportunity to call them to the worship of Allah alone. Why? Because they were polytheists.
And Yusuf – a prophet. So Yusuf said to them: "I have left," that is, "I have not accepted the religion of the people with whom I grew up", that is, those people with whom he grew up in the palace.

"Rather," he says, "wattaba'tu millata aba'i Ibrahima wa Ishaqa wa Ya'qub" – "but I have," he says, "remained following the religion of my great-grandfather Ibrahim, my grandfather Ishaq and my father Yaqub, and I have remained upon their religion."
He says: "It does not befit us to commit shirk with Allah, to ascribe partners to Allah." He says: "That is from Allah's mercy towards us." Yusuf addresses them,

he says: "That is from Allah's mercy towards us." There is no greater blessing than guidance, dear brothers, there is no greater blessing than guidance. And that is why, when a person sees someone who has no guidance but has a lot of money, do not, dear brothers, let a person fret too much. Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, says to His Messenger: "Wa la tamuddanna 'aynayka ila ma matta'na bihi azwajan minhum zahratal-hayatid-dunya li naftinahum fih" – do not let your eyes stray to what they have

of the dunya (this world); We gave it to them – why? – in order to test them. And what Allah will give you, the provision (rizq), is better and more lasting. What Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, will give the believer in the Hereafter (akhirah) is much better and more lasting. That is why a person should not fret too much.

Provision, wallahu… [unclear] He gives to whom He wills. So he says, he says: "Wattaba'tu millata aba'i Ibrahima wa Ishaqa wa Ya'qub, ma kana lana an nushrika billahi min shay'. Dhalika min fadlillahi 'alayna" – that is from Allah's favour towards us – "wa 'alan-nas" – and, he says, towards people. So guidance, guidance is among Allah's blessings, among the greatest of Allah's blessings, that is, Allah's greatest blessing towards people. "ولكن أكثر الناس لا يشكرون" – but most people [unclear]

[unclear] verses, many verses Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, [unclear]: "ولكن أكثر الناس لا يؤمنون" – but most people do not believe [unclear] "ولكن أكثرهم لا يعقلون" – but most people do not reflect, do not think, do not use their brains. So, as we said, Yusuf wanted something more, to tell them something more, not just to interpret their dreams; he wanted something more. In the Sharia this

is called, well, it is said, "al-jawabul-hakim", it is said, the wise answer: when the one who is asked does not aim only at the question, the answer to the question, but at something more. And in the hadiths of the Prophet, or in the Sunnah of the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam (peace be upon him), we have quite a few of these examples, where, when the companions ask him, they say: "O Messenger, if we happened to be," they say, "at sea, on a ship, and we have only," they say, "a little water," they say, "should we use that water for ablution (wudu) or should we keep it for drinking and make ablution with sea water?"
What does the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, say? He says: "Huwat-tahuru ma'uhu" – he says: sea water is pure, so use it, so use it for ablution.
And, he says, those creatures that are in the water, he says, are halal for you, even if they are dead. Meaning, fish is halal even if it has died, even if it is dead.

Meaning, it is halal for a Muslim to take it, to eat it. So the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, gave them something more. So too Yusuf: they asked him about dreams, but Yusuf – what? – saw an opportunity to call them. So he gave them a somewhat fuller answer. So we see, dear brothers, whenever a person sees an opportunity – especially we here who come, who pray, who know of Allah, who know of the Prophet, who know of Islam – we should seize that opportunity: when we see that we can influence someone at a given moment, we should influence him at once.
As Yusuf did. Meaning, he saw the opportunity and immediately began to call, to call these two to the worship of Allah. So, it says, he says: "These false deities of yours,

all sorts of them – are they," he says, "better than Allah, the Almighty, the One?" They are not better. This is an affirmative question, where the speaker does not want information; Yusuf did not want that either. Yusuf knew that Allah is better, but he wanted these two to affirm what he was asking.
Now someone will ask: "All right, Effendi, why are you talking about this here? There are no people here who, I don't know, worship other deities. We all worship Allah," and so on.
It is not, dear brothers, only about when we see a person bowing down to some idol, and so on. A person can easily take his desires as a deity: money, the dunya.

Allah mentions this in the Qur'an, addressing the Prophet, and says… He says: "Have you seen," He says, "O Messenger of Allah, the one who has taken his desires as his deity?" So everything a person submits to – whether his soul, his desires, his dunya or someone else – that, meaning, is what he has taken as a deity.

Why? He does not follow what Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, has commanded him, and His Messenger, but precisely what his soul wants. So whatever his soul wants, whatever his soul commands him, he does it. So he has taken his soul, his desires, as a deity.

Yusuf, alayhis-salam, further says: "What you worship here in Egypt is nothing but names, false names, false deities, which you and your fathers have named, for which Allah has sent down no proof." Allah did not send down any proof that you should worship them, there is no proof, Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, did not say "worship this and that"; rather Allah – what does He say? – Allah has commanded that you worship Him alone,

"wa bil-walidayni ihsana" – and that you do good to your parents. "Dhalikad-dinul-qayyim" – he says: that is the right religion, such is the religion – "wa lakinna aktharan-nasi la ya'lamun" – but, he says, most people do not know, [unclear], he says, most people do not know. So here Yusuf finished with them as far as da'wah, as far as the call is concerned.

So here Yusuf called them to the worship of Allah. Yusuf further says – now he returns to the interpretation of the dreams: "Ya sahibayis-sijni" – he says: "O you fellow prisoners," or "O you who stay in prison together with me."
"Amma ahadukuma fa yasqi rabbahu khamra" – one of you two will, he says, be cupbearer to the king and will be close to the king. One of you two – will be close to the king.

Why? Because he saved his life. So the king will take him out of prison, return him to the palace, and he will be close to him, his associate. "Wa ammal-akharu fa yuslabu fa ta'kulut-tayru min ra'sih" – and, he says, the other will be executed
and crucified, and birds will peck at his head, his brain, that is, they will eat from his head, from his brain, and so on, and so on, his body.

So, he says, as far as the interpretation of these dreams is concerned, that is done. And it will be so. And it was so. And there you have it, dear brothers, how cleverly and kindly Yusuf put it to them… He did not say: "You, you will be killed, you will be saved."

Rather he said "one of you", he did not want, did not want to say it directly, but "one of you". That is from Yusuf's fine character (akhlaq) and from his, meaning, sharp-wittedness. Imagine if he had told a man: "You will be executed," and the other: "You will be saved."

The man would probably have had a nervous breakdown and so on. Instead he says "one of you", and you will see which one it will be. It goes on: Yusuf, alayhis-salam, when he had interpreted these dreams for them, said to the one he knew 100% would be saved – whom he knew one hundred percent would be saved and return to the palace: "Udhkurni 'inda rabbik" – he says: "Mention me to the king, since you will be among his close people.

Mention me to him. Say: there is a man here in prison to whom a great injustice has been done." But, it says, Shaytan made this young man forget about Yusuf. And he left the prison and forgot about Yusuf, forgot what Yusuf had told him.

There are mufassirun (Qur'an commentators) who nevertheless say: Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, punished Yusuf because he did not rely on Allah, but relied, they say, on this young man to mention him to the king. But that is far-fetched. It is far-fetched that Yusuf would forget about Allah.

You will see later, in sha Allah – we will talk about it tomorrow – when Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, says about this young man: "Waddakara ba'da ummah" – He says: and, it says, this young man remembered Yusuf. He remembered after some time, he remembered Yusuf. And it cannot be [unclear] who forgot to remember.

It cannot be Yusuf who remembered, since it is not mentioned that he forgot anything. Because he was mentioning Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, the whole time, and the whole time he relied on Allah. You yourselves know these verses that we have mentioned.
So after that Yusuf remained in prison a certain number of years. "Bid'" in Arabic means from 3 to 10 years. And, it is said, most scholars hold that he remained in prison for 7 years.

Imagine, dear brothers, 7 years in prison after this. This was a message to Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, and to all of us as well. Because this surah came at a time when things were hardest for Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, when his wife Khadijah passed away, when the Quraysh boycotted him, i.e. when the Quraysh boycotted the Muslims, neither buying from them nor selling to them, etc.

So this surah was deliberately, well, sent as motivation for the Prophet. We see what happened to Yusuf. So, O Messenger, you see how Yusuf spent seven years in prison, and after that Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, raised him up. So He will raise you too, O Messenger of Allah. Only what is needed? That a person be patient.

First, God-fearing. Meaning, this recipe for success is God-consciousness (taqwa) and patience. And then, after that, after that comes success, one hundred percent. Here we stop; in sha Allah, tomorrow we continue.
May Allah grant you every good. As-salamu alaykum wa rahmatullahi wa barakatuh.
